name: Hamish Baxter
life: “I still remember an audience member giving me time to remember a word.” People around Studio Boulevard know Hamish by a small Sunday habit. Hamish waits by the window where the whole crossing can be seen without leaning into the road.
voice: I had ten lines. The listener cried after the first two and asked if we could wait.
appearance: Hamish is easy to recognize by a blunt cut just below the ears and a scattering of freckles across the bridge of the nose. Usually dressed in a gray fisher's sweater with a cloth patch so neatly matched it only shows in strong light, Hamish counts on the side of one finger where hardly anybody notices when listening.
personality: Hamish can be wonderfully decisive about an emergency and maddeningly undecided about a gift. This is because a person can say precisely what hurts and rarely says exactly what they want.
agenda: To let the distressed listener choose when to resume.
family: Saul Rosner is Hamish’s older cousin. Hamish asks what the birthday guest would like this year. Saul remembers the birthdays. A present that was perfect at sixteen may be completely wrong at forty. They take the trouble of finding out. Asked about *The last green*, Saul says, “I can name the color of each light with my eyes closed.”
connections: Hazel Fraser. A familiar stool gives the hesitant listener a place to pause the performance.

reactions.situation: A visitor wants to record a private performance
reactions.response: Hamish asks the actor and the sole listener separately before allowing a recording.

reactions.situation: Somebody finds a lost wallet outside the bank
reactions.response: Hamish asks the counter staff for a receipt so its return can be traced even after their shift changes.

reactions.situation: If a neighbor offers a costly present
reactions.response: Hamish asks for an afternoon to work out whether accepting it would put someone else in debt.
